title: Finish Time of Tasks I
summary: Given n tasks forming a tree with task 0 as the root, and an array of base completion times, calculate the finish time for each task.
statement: Given n tasks forming a tree with task 0 as the root, and an array of base completion times, calculate the finish time for each task. For leaf tasks, the finish time is their base time. For non-leaf tasks, the finish time is the maximum child finish time plus the difference between the maximum and minimum child finish times plus the task's base time.
constraints: Directed edges parent-child form a rooted tree at task zero.
A leaf finishes at its base time; an internal task finishes at latest child + (latest-earliest) + its base time.
hints: Child subtrees must finish before their parent formula can be evaluated.
Use postorder recursion to collect all child finish times.
Return base time for leaves; otherwise latest+(latest-earliest)+base.
Postorder computes each dependency exactly once before its parent.
editorial: Postorder computes each dependency exactly once before its parent.

tests.explanation: The chain finishes bottom-up at 3, then 8, then 17.
Child times four and seven give root finish 7+(7-4)+2=12.
